why-ddd.title: Why DDD
why-ddd.objective: Explain why changing an anemic model keeps getting more expensive and how a rich model contains the cost.

ubiquitous-language.title: Ubiquitous language
ubiquitous-language.objective: Spot ambiguous terms and agree on one vocabulary that experts and code use alike.

event-storming.title: Event Storming
event-storming.objective: Discover a domain by ordering events in time and adding commands, actors, policies, systems, read models and aggregates.

bounded-contexts.title: Bounded contexts
bounded-contexts.objective: Draw context boundaries and justify where a model stops being valid.

context-map.title: Context map
context-map.objective: Choose and justify a relationship pattern between contexts, including an anticorruption layer against an external system.

subdomains.title: Subdomains
subdomains.objective: Classify subdomains as core, supporting or generic and decide where to invest effort.

tactical-building-blocks.title: Tactical building blocks
tactical-building-blocks.objective: Model with value objects, entities and aggregates that protect their invariants, and expose events, repositories, factories and services.

functional-modeling.title: Functional modeling
functional-modeling.objective: Express the domain with constrained types, states as types, workflows as pipelines and errors as values, and compare it with the classic approach.

architecture.title: Architecture around the domain
architecture.objective: Isolate the domain with ports and adapters and justify the dependency rule.

evolution.title: Evolution
evolution.objective: Refactor toward deeper understanding when a new requirement arrives and recognize implicit concepts.

why.ball-of-mud.title: Big ball of mud
why.ball-of-mud.summary: A system without clear structure where everything depends on everything and nobody dares to touch anything.

why.anemic-model.title: Anemic model
why.anemic-model.summary: Objects that only hold data while business rules are scattered across services and screens.

why.cost-of-change.title: Cost of change
why.cost-of-change.summary: How many places must be touched to apply a business change and how easy it is to miss one.

why.model-driven.title: Model-driven design
why.model-driven.summary: Letting the code express the business model and not the other way around: model and code evolve together.

lang.ubiquitous-language.title: Ubiquitous language
lang.ubiquitous-language.summary: A shared language born from conversations with experts that appears the same on boards, docs and code.

lang.glossary.title: Living glossary
lang.glossary.summary: The list of domain terms with their meaning, growing and being corrected with every conversation.

lang.ambiguity.title: Ambiguity
lang.ambiguity.summary: One word with different meanings depending on who uses it; it is flagged and resolved, not ignored.

storm.events.title: Domain events
storm.events.summary: Facts that already happened, written in the past tense, forming the business timeline (orange).

storm.commands.title: Commands
storm.commands.summary: Decisions or intentions that cause events; some are refused by the business (blue).

storm.actors.title: Actors
storm.actors.summary: The people or roles who issue the commands (pale yellow).

storm.policies.title: Policies
storm.policies.summary: Reactive rules of the form “whenever X happens, then do Y” (lilac).

storm.external-systems.title: External systems
storm.external-systems.summary: Services outside the domain that receive or emit commands and events (pink).

storm.read-models.title: Read models
storm.read-models.summary: The information a person needs to see to decide their next command (green).

storm.aggregates.title: Aggregates
storm.aggregates.summary: What receives a command, protects its rules and produces events (large yellow).

context.bounded-context.title: Bounded context
context.bounded-context.summary: A boundary inside which a model and its language have a single coherent meaning.

context.term-translation.title: The term that changes
context.term-translation.summary: Crossing a boundary, the same word becomes another concept with other data and other rules.

map.context-map.title: Context map
map.context-map.summary: The picture of how contexts relate and who depends on whom.

map.customer-supplier.title: Customer / Supplier
map.customer-supplier.summary: Upstream and downstream coordinate: the customer can ask the supplier for changes.

map.conformist.title: Conformist
map.conformist.summary: The downstream accepts the upstream's model as is because it cannot influence it.

map.anticorruption-layer.title: Anticorruption layer
map.anticorruption-layer.summary: A translation at the boundary that keeps the foreign model from contaminating your own.

map.open-host-service.title: Open Host Service
map.open-host-service.summary: A context exposes an open, stable service for many to consume.

map.published-language.title: Published language
map.published-language.summary: A well-documented format for exchanging information between contexts.

map.shared-kernel.title: Shared kernel
map.shared-kernel.summary: Two contexts share a subset of the model and commit to changing it together.

map.partnership.title: Partnership
map.partnership.summary: Two teams succeed or fail together and coordinate their changes.

map.separate-ways.title: Separate ways
map.separate-ways.summary: Two contexts decide not to integrate because the cost outweighs the benefit.

strategy.core-domain.title: Core domain
strategy.core-domain.summary: What sets the business apart from others and deserves the best model and the best team.

strategy.supporting-subdomain.title: Supporting subdomain
strategy.supporting-subdomain.summary: Needed to operate but not a differentiator; built simply and to measure.

strategy.generic-subdomain.title: Generic subdomain
strategy.generic-subdomain.summary: A problem solved the same way for everyone; better to buy or reuse than to invent.

strategy.investment.title: Where to invest
strategy.investment.summary: Allocating effort by strategic value: build, buy or outsource.

tactical.value-object.title: Value object
tactical.value-object.summary: A value defined by its attributes, immutable and valid from the moment it exists.

tactical.entity.title: Entity
tactical.entity.summary: An object with its own identity that persists as its attributes change.

tactical.aggregate.title: Aggregate
tactical.aggregate.summary: A group of objects treated as a unit of consistency, with a root as the only way in.

tactical.invariant.title: Invariant
tactical.invariant.summary: A rule that must always hold; the aggregate rejects any command that would break it.

tactical.domain-event.title: Domain event
tactical.domain-event.summary: The record of something relevant that happened, published by the aggregate so others can react.

tactical.repository.title: Repository
tactical.repository.summary: A collection of aggregates that hides how and where they are stored.

tactical.factory.title: Factory
tactical.factory.summary: What creates complex objects already valid, so the rest need not know the details.

tactical.domain-service.title: Domain service
tactical.domain-service.summary: A business operation that does not naturally belong to any aggregate.

tactical.application-service.title: Application service
tactical.application-service.summary: Orchestrates a use case: loads aggregates, gives them orders and saves the result, holding no rules.

functional.constrained-types.title: Constrained types
functional.constrained-types.summary: Small types that only admit legal values, built with a constructor that can fail.

functional.states-as-types.title: States as types
functional.states-as-types.summary: Each lifecycle state is a distinct type with exactly the data that belongs to it.

functional.illegal-states.title: Making illegal states unrepresentable
functional.illegal-states.summary: Designing types so that an invalid state cannot even be written.

functional.pipeline.title: Workflows as pipelines
functional.pipeline.summary: A business process as a chain of stages where each transforms the previous one's type.

functional.errors-as-values.title: Errors as values
functional.errors-as-values.summary: Expected failures are returned as results that must be handled, not as surprise exceptions.

architecture.layers.title: Layers
architecture.layers.summary: Separating the domain from the interface, application and infrastructure so each changes for its own reason.

architecture.hexagonal.title: Hexagonal architecture
architecture.hexagonal.summary: The domain at the center and everything else connected through ports.

architecture.ports-adapters.title: Ports and adapters
architecture.ports-adapters.summary: A port is what the domain needs; an adapter is a concrete way to provide it.

architecture.dependency-rule.title: Dependency rule
architecture.dependency-rule.summary: Dependencies always point toward the domain, never the other way around.

evolution.implicit-concepts.title: Implicit concepts
evolution.implicit-concepts.summary: Something everyone mentions but the model never named, showing up as patches and exceptions.

evolution.refactoring-toward-insight.title: Refactoring toward deeper insight
evolution.refactoring-toward-insight.summary: Changing the model not just to add a feature but because we now understand the business better.

evolution.breakthrough.title: A breakthrough
evolution.breakthrough.summary: The moment a new concept suddenly simplifies many rules that seemed separate.
